title: Book One · Chapter 54: Seven at the Green Gate
story:
On Tuesday, Ronan turns seven.

He wakes early. Mum is still asleep. The room is the same size. His feet don't reach the end of the bed. He checks anyway.

Dad puts a clean paper seven beside his bowl. Mum brings out one round sweet pancake. One edge sticks out a little. Mum turns that side toward Ronan. He still likes the shape.

Ronan reaches for it. “Keep it for later,” she says.

He has school first. Mei gives him a card with a black cat on a green gate. The cat has four clear feet and a fine tail. It sits up high on the gate. It looks down at everyone below.

“I can't come this afternoon,” she says. “My aunt's waiting.”

“I remember. Thank you.”

He keeps the card flat inside his reading book. He doesn't fold it to make it fit a pocket.

After school, Leo and Jun come to the yard. Bo arrives later with Mr Han. Mr Han stays for tea with Mrs Lan. Mum agreed on pickup times with all the parents. There is no room for the red bicycle inside. Mr Han keeps it near him at the front.

Jun brings his paper game. Leo brings three smooth stones. Two are for the game. The other is a spare. Bo brings his wooden top. “I'll show you again,” he says. “I'll do it slowly this time.”

Ronan chooses the chalk game first. He explains the circle and the waiting place. Leo loses the first turn. Now he wants to change the points.

“After this game,” Ronan says. “Then we can try your rules.”

Leo looks at the other boys. The boys agree. They finish their first game. Then they can try Leo's rules.

The black cat walks through the chalk circle. Everyone stops. It sits in the winning place for the stones.

“Highest score,” Bo says.

“Very poor manners,” Mrs Lan says from her chair.

The cat stays in the circle. They move to the paper game. No one tries to pull its tail. Jun is best at this game. He keeps the same rules for everyone. He knows the safe squares. He moves his stones to them.

The friends are still there. Dad comes home. He has a small paper bag with two oranges. He gives the oranges to Mum. The boys are counting their last points. Dad tells Mum the news quietly first.

Then they call Ronan over.

“Three trial mornings at Mr Sun's,” Dad says. “I start next Monday. We agreed on the pay and the hours.”

“So you have work?”

“For those mornings. Then we'll see about more.”

Ronan almost calls it Dad's new shop. Then he remembers Mr Sun. That is Mr Sun's shop, not Dad's. Dad has a place to work for three mornings. Ronan smiles at the news. Three mornings are a good start.

The friends go home at their agreed times. “Thank you for the games,” Ronan says to each friend. He doesn't count the gifts in front of them. Mei's card goes beside the old-house drawing. Ronan can see it from his bed.

In the evening, Mrs Lan joins them for noodles. Mum cuts the pancake into four pieces. Dad puts a candle on a saucer. The paper seven is well away from it. Then he lights the candle.

Ronan makes a wish and blows it out. He keeps the wish to himself. It is a wish. He makes no promise about it.

They finish the noodles. Ronan carries the empty bowls to the kitchen. The gate outside is the same green gate as yesterday. He is seven now. His friends are at home now. His four coins are in the tea box. Dad has a starting time for work on Monday. Ronan stacks the bowls beside the sink. Mum comes to help him wash them.
studyGuide:
---

重点表达：pancake＝煎饼；rules＝规则；trial＝试工；candle＝蜡烛。

理解问题：

1. 生日聚会中每个朋友贡献了什么？
2. Dad 带回了什么消息，这消息有哪些限制？
